title: tseLCA Workflow
text: Latent class analysis (LCA) groups observations unobserved classes set categorical indicators. Researchers usually also want know classes relate variables: covariates predict class membership, distal outcomes classes predict. tseLCA three-step estimation: Measurement model. Estimate latent classes indicators alone (tse_lca()). Classification. Assign observations classes quantify classification error (tse_classify()). Structural model. Relate classes covariates (tse_covariate()) distal outcomes (tse_distal()), correcting classification error Step 2. measurement model fixed structural variable enters, covariates outcomes change classes mean. main reason prefer three-step one-step estimation, indicators, covariates, outcomes modeled jointly class solution can shift every change structural specification. Assigning observations classes analyzing assignments, true classes, biases structural estimates toward zero; bias-adjusted estimators Bolck, Croon, Hagenaars (2004; “BCH”) Vermunt (2010; “ML”) remove bias, tseLCA adds standard errors account uncertainty Step-1 measurement model (Bakk, Oberski, Vermunt 2014). step returns object can inspected usual R tools (print(), summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), logLik(), AIC(), BIC(), predict(), plot()) moving next. one-call interface tseLCA() runs steps .

Outcomes can "gaussian" (class means common variance), "poisson", "binomial", "multinomial" (nominal). omnibus_test() tests whether outcome’s distribution differs across classes: nominal outcome, coef(fit, matrix = TRUE) gives class--category probability matrix:

Measurement model (tse_lca()). latent classes estimated indicators alone, number classes chosen class-enumeration table. Classification (tse_classify()). Observations assigned classes, classification error estimated. Structural model (tse_covariate(), tse_distal()). classes related covariates /distal outcomes, ML (Vermunt 2010) BCH (Bolck, Croon & Hagenaars 2004) correction classification error. measurement model fixed structural variable enters, covariates outcomes change classes mean. key difference one-step estimation (e.g. poLCA), class solution can shift every change structural model. standard errors structural estimates account uncertainty measurement model (Bakk, Oberski & Vermunt 2014). Measurement models estimated multilevLCA.

code: library(tseLCA)  # Simulated data: six binary indicators, a covariate Zp, and a distal outcome Zo d <- generate_data(n = 1000, separation = "high", scenario = "covariate", seed = 1) d$Zo <- draw_Zo(d$X, bk2018_params$distal_params)  # Step 1: choose the number of classes from the measurement model sel <- tse_lca(cbind(Y1, Y2, Y3, Y4, Y5, Y6) ~ 1, data = d, nclass = 1:4) sel m <- best_model(sel, criterion = "BIC")  # Step 2: classification cl <- tse_classify(m)  # Step 3: covariate and distal outcome models fc <- tse_covariate(cl, ~ Zp) summary(fc) fb <- tse_distal(fc, Zo ~ 1) summary(fb)  # The same model in one call fit <- tseLCA(cbind(Y1, Y2, Y3, Y4, Y5, Y6) ~ Zp | Zo, data = d, nclass = 3)

title: Three-step LCA estimation with covariates and/or distal outcomes — three_step
text: Fits three-step latent class model following steps: Measurement model: estimates latent class parameters (\(\pi\), \(\phi\)) using multilevLCA (Lyrvall et al., 2025). Classification-error matrix: computes posterior class probabilities T x T misclassification probability matrix \(P(W = s \mid X = t)\), standard errors corrected classification-error propagation (Bakk, Oberski & Vermunt, 2014). Structural model: estimates covariate effects using two-step starting values (Bakk & Kuha, 2018) /distal outcome means following Bakk, Tekle & Vermunt (2013), ML correction (Vermunt, 2010) BCH correction (Bolck, Croon & Hagenaars, 2004). See vignette("tseLCA", package = "tseLCA") worked example.

title: Relate latent classes to covariates (Step 3) — tse_covariate
text: Estimators (method): "ML" (default): bias-adjusted maximum likelihood estimator Vermunt (2010), treats assigned class indicator true class known classification-error probabilities. "BCH": Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars estimator (Bolck, Croon, Hagenaars 2004; Vermunt 2010), reweights assignments inverse classification-error matrix. "none": uncorrected three-step estimator (weighted multinomial logit assigned classes), biased toward zero; provided comparison. Standard errors (se): "corrected" (default) adds uncertainty Step-1 measurement model (Bakk, Oberski, Vermunt 2014) robust (sandwich) Step-3 variance; "robust" omits . "BCH" robust variance used, accounts Step-1 uncertainty weights (Vermunt 2010); "none" robust variance used.
